meaning: The cumulative preparation-capture interval is now explicitly defined without changing the 8192-byte cap or protocol schema.

counter_interval.start: Preparation owning boundary records the authenticated single-operation admission for this attempt's already-spent original materialization facet, before dispatching the MATERIALIZE_EXACT_SCENARIO_SOURCE request. That admission record is the single counter-origin event: open both counters at zero there, before any request or response byte of this exchange. Facet spending precedes the record; no cross-owner atomic transaction is claimed.
counter_interval.successful_end: The final physical byte of the complete terminal COMPILE_EXACT_SCENARIO response frame is captured by the owning boundary, including all actual framing and its entire mandatory workspace_state, compiler_identity, capture_and_reap and class_metadata. A successful attempt requires the complete valid COMPLETE response; child exit, payload parsing before frame completion, receipt authentication, new readiness OBSERVE request/response, handoff admission and cleanup completion are not this endpoint.
counter_interval.origin_basis: The materialization facet admission opens the one-shot effect attempt; independently, the existing shared deadline also begins there. Initial empty observation/request/response precede this effect boundary. Inner final local admission and first response byte are not new origins.

failure_end_cases.no_response_pending: Recorded irrevocable terminal attempt-abort event when no admitted ordinary operation response remains pending.
failure_end_cases.response_pending: First of: final byte of the last terminal ordinary response already admitted to this attempt; observed terminal channel closure/loss; original 10000ms hard preparation deadline. Count every observed partial/invalid ordinary byte until that event.
failure_end_cases.early_failure: A materialization failure/rejection or a later admission/compilation failure cannot wait for a nonexistent successful compile response. Apply the no-pending or pending-response case to the failed admitted operation; no second attempt or new counter is allowed.
failure_end_cases.cleanup_preemption: The cleanup barrier suppresses success immediately but does not close a pending ordinary response ledger. Its complete response suffix still belongs to the failed effect attempt, even if physically delivered after the barrier. Cleanup exchanges have their own ledger.
failure_end_cases.overflow: Overflow fails the attempt, never resets or forgives observed bytes; retain an exceeded/incomplete result and bounded partial/drain evidence. It never authorizes unbounded buffering, a late successful receipt or denial of mandatory independent cleanup.
failure_end_cases.loss_or_deadline: No terminal response is fabricated. Any still-unobserved ordinary suffix is unresolved, not an outside-budget exemption; the failed epoch cannot reopen or publish success. Mandatory cleanup remains independently bounded.

counter_interval.no_deadline_extension: The shared 5000ms attempt deadline is never renewed. Cancellation/reaping/capture closure and terminal drain remain clamped to original 10000ms hard bound; a failed result never appends a new preparation interval.
counter_interval.membership_rule: All ordinary effect request/response frames and any current observation invoked after origin but before the effect endpoint are members. Include actual framing in its own physical stream. Separately identifiable cleanup control/results retain cleanup membership even during preemption; pending ordinary bytes cannot be relabeled.
counter_interval.no_evidence_deferral: Every mandatory materialization/compile record must be complete in its own response before the endpoint. No chunking, delayed suffix, post-end receipt, observation or handoff may carry deferred effect response evidence to evade the unchanged cap.

fresh_readiness_observation.reason: Current eligibility is a fresh challenged observation of retained prepared workspace after completed effects; it is not a third preparation effect facet. Earlier in-attempt observations still count.
fresh_readiness_observation.required_tag: new complete challenged OBSERVE_* of prepared current state
fresh_readiness_observation.no_new_receipt_ordering_rule: Preserve all existing owner evidence/authentication checks. The byte endpoint does not require a receipt to precede CURRENT or force PREPARED to create the receipt it already requires.

initial_empty_observation.lifecycle_class: workspace initial eligibility before effect admission

cleanup.explicit_retry_scope: bounded same original identity only; permanent invalidity

independent_bounds.outer_custodian: Fixed 10000ms invocation deadline and <=8192-byte bounded response, no automatic retry. Explicit same-identity cleanup retry never restores readiness.
independent_bounds.retained_lifetime_gate: Exclusive workspace remains only until completion/abort/timeout/abandonment/upstream loss. No new retained lifetime numeric duration is preauthorized; future owner must enforce separately reviewed bounded lifetime policy before readiness.
independent_bounds.no_unbounded_exemption: Every outside observation/handoff uses existing per-operation time/frame/record/byte bounds and a separately reviewed finite retained lifetime policy before readiness. No universal numeric session/lifetime ceiling is invented or authorized here. Missing reviewed retained bounds denies readiness, not an unlimited channel.
independent_bounds.outside_diagnostics: Observation request/response ceilings do not independently bound arbitrary controller stderr or unsolicited output. Outside lifecycle traffic has no free diagnostic channel: unexpected/nonprotocol output fails closed; any future transport must prove finite capture bounds for all outer channels under its separately reviewed retained policy before operational eligibility. No new universal stderr number is invented. Candidate A retains empty successful controller stderr and its conditional session ceilings only.

conditional_candidate_A_only.reason: These are preserved reviewed candidate profile limits, not final transport or architecture selection; they never enlarge the 8192 effect cap.

cleanup.safety_capacity: Before ordinary admission the future transport must guarantee bounded independent/reserved cleanup capacity, including both cleanup exchanges and outer fallback. Normal effect capture may consume all 8192 bytes without spending cleanup capacity. If the channel cannot preserve this, deny ordinary admission; this requirement selects no transport.
cleanup.shared_channel: Separately identified cleanup frames are charged to cleanup and to any applicable retained-session ceiling once per ledger, not the ordinary effect ledger. Finishing an already-started ordinary response cannot convert its bytes to cleanup. Channel/normal-quota failure still invokes independent exact-generation outer teardown.
cleanup.reserves: For conditional candidate A, preserve two cleanup slots plus bounded cleanup/error response capacity within the 65536/session/64-request ceiling and the 10000ms cleanup time reserve. Ordinary admission cannot spend them. Existing independent cleanup and outer invocation bounds remain; reserves do not enlarge preparation capture.
cleanup.lost_inner_evidence: Removal and absence do not prove missing child reaping/EOF. Preserve unresolved components; no fabricated cleanup success.

stream_accounting.controller_stdin_requests: Report request payload/framing in its own direction. Semantic attempt membership does not turn stdin into captured outer stdout or stderr; no bidirectional sum or new cumulative stdin cap.
stream_accounting.controller_stdout_responses: Count each member response byte, including full embedded poststate and actual transport framing, once if mapped to outer stdout by a future transport. All partial/malformed/unframed/unexpected captured bytes during the effect epoch also count and deny success; missing labels do not exempt them. No omission, compression, alias or removal of duplicated evidence.
stream_accounting.controller_stderr: All bytes observed during the effect capture epoch count toward its separate 8192 stderr cap unless independently attributable to a separately bounded lifecycle channel. No untagged/shared stderr may be favorably relabeled as cleanup or observation. Empty successful candidate stderr is conditional precedent, not a new encoding shortcut.
stream_accounting.compiler_child_stdout: Separate <=2048 child capture; exact successful observed bytes=0. Metadata is already counted in compile response; do not add it twice.
stream_accounting.compiler_child_stderr: Separate <=2048 child capture; exact successful observed bytes=0. Metadata is already counted in compile response; do not add it twice.
stream_accounting.outer_custodian_channel: Separate fixed bounded cleanup invocation, no invented four-byte prefix and no charge to normal effect allowance.
stream_accounting.host_in_process_composed_evidence: Receipt authentication and provenance-preserving cleanup composition are not extra controller wire responses. A future serialization would require its actual bounded channel accounting, not a free exemption.
stream_accounting.payload_vs_physical: Freeze lifecycle membership here. Canonical semantic payload and actual physical framing are distinct; bytes on a capped physical stream include its real headers. No transport mapping is selected. Candidate A alone would put request+4 on stdin and response+4 on stdout.
stream_accounting.attempt_vs_session: Preparation attempt budget != retained controller session budget != workspace lifetime. One physical byte may be checked against nested applicable ceilings but is never added twice within one ledger. A larger session ceiling neither expands the effect allowance nor makes it a lifetime allowance.
stream_accounting.unattributed_or_late_bytes: A future channel must prove attribution and preserve bounded capture/closure; it cannot publish success by moving ordinary response suffixes past the endpoint. Unknown/lost/invalid bytes remain failure evidence, never an unlimited uncharged channel.

budget_arithmetic_consequence.reason: Fresh readiness observation is outside this effect capture. The already-known 6702-byte relaxed materialize+compile payload is only a lower relaxation; it does not prove an attainable semantic identity encoding or complete framed exchange can fit.
budget_arithmetic_consequence.inside_branch_not_selected: Had fresh observation been inside, 1R would seek impossibility confirmation using the already-known universal relaxed excess. That branch is not selected or proved here.
